_comment: Copy to config.json and replace every column name with the one in YOUR dataset. A role set to null is treated as absent. Keys starting with _ are ignored. Paths are relative to the working directory, else to this file.
_columns: role -> your column name. Required: author, views, and either age_hours or created_at + snapshot_utc. text is strongly recommended (text features and the text model). thread is null on purpose: map it only if it was set when the post was published (posted as a thread), never from the conversation as scraped later, where self-replies added after a post took off make it post-publication information.
_feature_columns: Optional: your precomputed text features, by kit feature name. Used only when text_feature_source is 'columns' or there is no text. score_drafts.py always derives features from draft text, so keep 'derive' unless the report's agreement table shows your columns match.
_extra: Other content features to use as-is, e.g. visual features present for a subset (NaN elsewhere). Only columns known when the post is published. Never list followers, engagement, clicks, scores/ranks, snapshot or age columns: train.py refuses them (also in feature_columns).

target._age_adjust: none | loglinear | spline. Off by default. For a wide age window (e.g. age_tolerance_hours 12): models log(views+1) on log(age_hours) (or a natural spline of it, age_spline_df) with author fixed effects and the content features as controls (age_adjust_controls 'features'; 'none' = age only), moves every post to age_hours, then builds the target. Age is never a model feature. See README 'Wide age window'.

models._drop_top_authors: K > 0: re-estimate effects without the K authors with the most posts at that level (CLI --drop-top-authors K --drop-effect opener=number). drop_top_effects empty = every effect whose CI excludes 0.
